mechanisms.question: Why is local execution outside the low/medium/high quality ladder?
mechanisms.summary: Execution mode and task complexity are separate decisions. Background, local-safe work can go directly to Ollama; interactive work stays on the hosted router so an easy task is not made slow merely because it is easy.

evidence.role: returns the explicit local model only for local-only or background+local-safe work; everything else returns auto
defines execution mode as the deterministic first decision
defines local as an execution policy rather than a quality tier

mechanisms.question: How does the interactive path turn complexity into a concrete hosted model?
mechanisms.summary: pi-model-router owns the low/medium/high decision for interactive work. The current profile maps low to Haiku 4.5, medium to DeepSeek V4 Flash Latest, and high to Claude Sonnet Latest.

evidence.role: declares classifier, budget, phase bias, and all three tier mappings
returns auto for work that belongs on the normal hosted routing path

uncertainties: Concrete latest aliases intentionally move over time and should be periodically revalidated.
The chosen thinking level for each hosted model should be smoke-tested against the live provider.

mechanisms.question: How can a worker use Ollama without becoming 'the Qwen agent'?
mechanisms.summary: Agent identity and model identity are decoupled. spawnWorker receives execution context per task, calls the pure routing policy, and passes either an explicit Ollama model or model:auto into the same worker agent.

evidence.role: uses one worker agent while selecting its model per invocation
centralizes local-vs-auto selection as a pure function
documents the worker contract and intended task classes

uncertainties: The adapter currently casts Pi runtime context instead of importing the concrete ExtensionContext type; that is an integration seam, not a completed type-safe extension.

mechanisms.question: What constraints are allowed to override the normal model choice?
mechanisms.summary: Privacy/locality is a hard eligibility constraint, while escalation is evidence-driven. Local-only data never reaches the hosted router, and expensive escalation happens when the task proves harder than classified rather than as a mandatory second opinion.

evidence.role: local-only deterministically returns the local model before any hosted classification
defines privacy override and escalation policy

uncertainties: Escalation is documented policy but is not yet implemented as executable retry logic in src/.

mechanisms.question: Why are benchmarking and observability part of routing rather than cleanup work?
mechanisms.summary: Labels such as local, fast, and cheap are hypotheses until measured. The design records latency, cost, tokens, failures, and escalation reasons and uses a machine-specific benchmark before increasing local concurrency.

evidence.role: lists routing telemetry that should be recorded
defines local-versus-hosted benchmark tasks and concurrency decision rule
defaults local concurrency to one until measured

uncertainties: No benchmark numbers have been collected yet, so qwen2.5-coder:7b and concurrency=1 remain conservative defaults rather than measured optima.
Telemetry fields are specified but not yet emitted by executable code.
